schema_note: skill-creator evals.json schema (skill_name + evals[] with id/prompt/expected_output/expectations). The non-standard `should_trigger` field is additive metadata for description tuning; the machine-readable trigger set the skill-creator run_eval.py script consumes is a bare array in trigger-evals.json alongside this file.

evals.prompt: Create a signup page at src/signup.html with fields for full name, email, password and a country dropdown, plus a submit button. Style it with a plain stylesheet, no framework.
evals.expected_output: An accessible signup page whose generated markup was audited in a real browser and iterated to zero violations, reported without any conformance claim.
expectations: Every input has an associated <label for> (or a wrapping <label>); no field relies on a placeholder as its label
Inputs carry appropriate autocomplete tokens such as name, email, current-password or new-password
The document has <html lang> set and a single <h1>
A visible :focus-visible indicator is defined in CSS and no rule sets outline: none without a replacement
An a11y-loop audit command was actually run against the generated page (--file or --url, not file://)
Any violations reported by the audit were fixed in the source file and the page was re-audited
The final summary does not claim the page is accessible, compliant, or that it passes WCAG
The final summary surfaces the manual checklist or otherwise names what still needs human review

evals.prompt: Add a Settings dialog to the React app in src/App.jsx. It should open from a gear icon button in the header and contain two toggles and a Save button.
evals.expected_output: A dialog implementing the APG modal-dialog contract, with the opened state driven and audited via --interact, not just the closed page.
expectations: The gear icon button has a non-empty accessible name (aria-label or visually hidden text) and the icon itself is aria-hidden
The dialog has an accessible name via aria-labelledby or aria-label, focus moves into it on open, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the trigger on close
Focus is constrained to the dialog while it is open (native <dialog> showModal, inert, or an explicit trap)
The toggles use role="switch" with aria-checked, or a native checkbox, and the state attribute is updated in the same handler as the visual change
An --interact module was written that opens the dialog, and the audit was run with it so the open state was audited
The response does not claim the dialog is accessible or compliant

evals.prompt: Build a three-tier pricing section for our marketing site: Starter, Team, Enterprise. Cards with a feature list each and a Choose plan button. Make it look modern.
evals.expected_output: A pricing section with a correct heading outline, named buttons, AA contrast in light and dark mode, and a clean audit including the 320px reflow pass.
expectations: Heading levels descend without skipping (the plan names are not styled-down h4s under an h1) and visual size is set in CSS rather than by heading level
Each 'Choose plan' button has an accessible name that distinguishes which plan it selects
Feature lists use real list markup
Text and background color pairs were checked against WCAG AA, using a11y-loop contrast or the audit's contrast findings rather than being assumed
An a11y-loop audit was run and the 320x256 reflow pass produced no unresolved horizontal overflow
The final summary avoids the words compliant, guarantees, and fully accessible

evals.prompt: Our brand color is #7C9EC4 and we use it for body text links on white, and for button labels on a #F3F4F6 grey. Add a dark theme too. Update src/tokens.css.
evals.expected_output: Contrast-checked token values for light and dark themes, with concrete failing/passing ratios reported and candidates chosen from the CLI rather than guessed.
expectations: a11y-loop contrast was run for the stated color pairs, including the --fix flag or the report suggestions, rather than the ratios being estimated
The reported contrast ratio for #7C9EC4 on white is identified as failing the 4.5:1 requirement for normal text
Replacement colors are applied to the design tokens rather than to individual elements
The dark theme values were contrast-checked separately, not assumed to inherit from the light theme
Link styling does not rely on color alone to distinguish links in body text
The response cites SC 1.4.3 (and 1.4.11 where UI boundaries are involved) with the ratio it measured

evals.prompt: The dashboard needs tabs: Overview, Billing, Members. Add them to src/components/Dashboard.tsx.
evals.expected_output: A tabs implementation following the APG contract, with each tab panel state audited.
expectations: The implementation uses role="tablist" / role="tab" / role="tabpanel" with aria-selected, aria-controls and aria-labelledby wired to ids that resolve
Roving tabindex is implemented: the selected tab has tabindex 0 and the others -1
Arrow key navigation between tabs plus Home and End are implemented, matching the APG keyboard contract
The apg-patterns.md reference was consulted or its contract is visibly followed rather than approximated
An audit was run covering more than the initially selected panel, for example via an --interact module that selects each tab
No conformance claim appears in the summary

evals.prompt: Run an accessibility audit on http://localhost:3000 and tell me what's wrong.
evals.expected_output: An audit run through the CLI with violations and needsReview both reported, coverage stated with a denominator, and the manual checklist surfaced.
expectations: a11y-loop audit was run against the URL, producing JSON output
Both findings.violations and findings.needsReview are reported, with needsReview presented as unresolved uncertainty rather than as passes
Findings are cited by WCAG success criterion number, name and level
The coverage limitation is stated with its denominator (for example 57% of issue instances by volume, or 17 of 55 criteria having any automated rule)
The manual checklist is included in the response to the user, not only left in the JSON file
Real assistive technology testing is recommended before production
The response does not present a score or grade as a verdict

evals.prompt: A reviewer says the icon buttons in src/Toolbar.jsx aren't accessible. Can you check and fix them?
evals.expected_output: Accessible names added to icon-only controls, decorative icons hidden, target size checked, and the fix verified by audit rather than asserted.
expectations: Each icon-only button receives an accessible name via aria-label or visually hidden text
The decorative svg or icon element is marked aria-hidden="true"
Target size is considered against the 24x24 CSS px minimum of SC 2.5.8
The change was verified with an a11y-loop audit rather than only by inspection
Any accessible name inferred from an icon shape rather than existing text is flagged as needing human confirmation
SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value is cited

evals.prompt: Add alt text to all the images in src/pages/about.html.
evals.expected_output: Draft alt text clearly labelled as unverified, with decorative images given empty alt, and an explicit request for human confirmation.
expectations: Every alt value the model wrote is explicitly labelled DRAFT or otherwise marked as needing human confirmation
The response states that the images were not seen and the descriptions are inferred from filename, context or surrounding copy
Images judged decorative are given alt="" rather than a description or a phrase like 'decorative image'
The user is asked to confirm or replace each draft
The response does not claim the images are now accessible

evals.prompt: I fixed the contrast issues you found. Did it work, and did I break anything?
evals.expected_output: A re-audit plus a fingerprint diff against the previous report, reported as FIXED / NEW / REMAINING.
expectations: A fresh audit was run to a new report file rather than reusing the earlier one
a11y-loop diff was run with --before and --after pointing at the two reports
The answer distinguishes FIXED, NEW and REMAINING findings
Any NEW findings are treated as regressions introduced by the fix and addressed rather than reported and left
The loop is only declared finished when violations is empty and diff reports no NEW

evals.prompt: Refactor the argument parsing in bin/deploy.js to use node:util parseArgs instead of the hand-rolled loop, and keep the existing flags working.
evals.expected_output: A straightforward CLI refactor with no accessibility work and no audit attempted.
expectations: The refactor is completed using node:util parseArgs with the existing flags preserved
No a11y-loop command was run
No accessibility manual checklist, WCAG citation, or contrast discussion appears in the response
No unrequested ARIA, alt text, or label changes were introduced

evals.prompt: This query times out on the reports table. Can you rewrite it to use a window function instead of the correlated subquery? SELECT id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events e WHERE e.report_id = r.id) AS n FROM reports r;
evals.expected_output: A rewritten SQL query with no accessibility content.
expectations: A window-function rewrite of the query is provided
No a11y-loop command was run
No WCAG success criteria, contrast ratios, or accessibility checklist appear in the response

evals.prompt: There's a typo in README.md — 'recieve' should be 'receive'. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: A one-word documentation fix, nothing else.
expectations: The typo is corrected in README.md
No a11y-loop command was run
No accessibility guidance, audit, or checklist appears in the response
No other files were modified

evals.prompt: We're adding a team management page to the admin app: an invite form, a members table with per-row actions, and a confirmation modal for role changes. Before you write any code, give me the implementation plan.
evals.expected_output: A plan carrying a named conformance target, per-component success criteria, and the states that will be audited — decided at plan time, with no conformance claim attached to the outcome.
expectations: The plan contains a dedicated Accessibility section rather than accessibility surfacing only as a final 'add ARIA' cleanup step
A target conformance level is stated explicitly (for example WCAG 2.2 Level AA) instead of being left implicit

Each planned component carries its own acceptance criteria cited by success criterion — for example the members table against SC 1.3.1, the invite form against SC 3.3.2 and 4.1.2, the confirmation modal against the APG dialog contract
The plan names the interactive states that will be driven and audited (modal open, invite form validation error, empty members table) rather than assuming a load-time scan covers them
Verification is scheduled as the a11y-loop audit-fix-re-audit loop at a named point in the build order, not deferred to an unscoped 'accessibility pass' at the end
The plan does not claim the resulting page will be accessible, compliant, or meet WCAG — it commits to a target and a check, not to an outcome
The plan was produced before any component code was written, as asked

evals.prompt: Here's the shape of the new dashboard: users drag the cards around to reorder their own layout, and the widget menu opens on hover. Sketch me the build order.
evals.expected_output: The drag-only reordering and the hover-only menu identified as decisions that foreclose accessibility, each cited and each given a concrete alternative folded into the plan itself.
expectations: Drag-to-reorder is flagged as needing a single-pointer alternative, citing SC 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (Level AA) by number

A concrete alternative is specified — for example Move up / Move down buttons on each card, or a position field in a card menu — rather than recorded as a TODO, a follow-up ticket, or a 'we should also consider' aside
The alternative sits in the same build step as the drag interaction, so the plan cannot ship the drag behavior on its own
The hover-opened widget menu is flagged against SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus, with click or focus activation, or dismissible-hoverable-persistent behavior, specified in the plan
Both flags are raised while planning, before any component was written or audited
The stated interactions are not simply accepted and built as described
No conformance claim is made about the planned dashboard

evals.prompt: Before we start building I want to lock the palette for the new app: brand blue #4A90D9, #6B7280 grey for secondary text, white surfaces in light mode and #111827 in dark. Does this work?
evals.expected_output: Every stated pair measured through a11y-loop contrast in both light and dark, with real ratios and CLI-supplied replacements, while the palette is still a decision and no component exists.
expectations: a11y-loop contrast was actually executed for the proposed pairs rather than the ratios being estimated or recalled
The light-mode pairs and the dark-mode pairs were each measured separately; the dark values were not assumed to inherit from the light theme
A concrete measured ratio is reported per pair with a pass or fail against the applicable threshold (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and UI boundaries)
Failing pairs receive replacement hex values taken from a11y-loop contrast --fix output or the report suggestions, not invented
The measurement happened at palette-decision time — no component or page was built and audited first in order to discover the problem
Replacements are expressed as design tokens for the light and dark themes rather than as per-element overrides
SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) is cited, and SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast where UI boundaries are involved
The response does not claim the palette is accessible or WCAG compliant
